answers.reasoning: The source motivation is learning regularities from data and experience where exhaustive rules become difficult. No guarantee for arbitrary unfamiliar objects follows.
The source explicitly identifies expert systems with human-authored if-then-else domain rules, unlike the three data-learning alternatives.
The described gap is translating holistic human recognition into executable pixel-level rules, not impossibility of representing an image numerically.
A new spam pattern can need a new or revised rule; the source universal entire-rewrite statement is too strong. An extension can preserve existing rules.
The code lowercases the message, then checks BLACKLIST in order. free money matches before click here and returns immediately.
Blacklist order is free money, click here, win prize, urgent, regardless of positions in the email. The first matching list entry is free money.
Python string membership is substring membership. insurgent contains urgent starting at index 3, so the final listed token matches.
Lowercasing does not create free money, click here, win prize or urgent. The source calls this an evasive spam variant while the rule returns NOT SPAM.
The format specifier left-aligns to a minimum width of 20 and does not truncate a longer result. The slice selects indices 0 through 54, at most 55 characters.
The actual grayscale bar labels 0 black and 255 white. Those values are intensities, not target labels or grid sizes.
There are 64 independent positions with 256 choices each, so 256^64=(2^8)^64=2^512 arrays.
The inspected eight rows each have eight entries. Row-major flattening gives 64 entries beginning 0,0,180,220.
New-data prediction applies learned regularities. Generalization accuracy is an empirical question, not true by the definition of unseen data.
The fit call uses only training features and labels. The test arrays are separate held-out examples for evaluation, not additional training columns.
The integer random_state fixes the randomized data split under the same data and implementation. It is not a neighbor count, target label or accuracy optimizer.
37/38=0.9736842105 and percentage formatting with zero decimal places produces 97%. Independently reproduced with scikit-learn 1.8.0.
The actual final line calls model.score(X_test,y_test), then formats the resulting accuracy. No explicit model.predict call appears on that page.
The first comparison 4.9<5 is true, and its return setosa ends the function before the long petal is checked.
Both strict comparisons fail at equality, 5<5 false and 2.5<2.5 false, so the else return is versicolor.
Only setosa and versicolor string literals occur in return branches. virginica is never predicted by this fixed function.
The first snippet visibly passes n_neighbors=1; the comparison snippet passes n_neighbors=5. The common seed does not make them equal.
fit receives in-memory feature and target arrays; the shown code has no network upload. The source phrase upload data in model means feed data here.
No terrain output labels are provided and similarity is used to group observations, which is the stated unsupervised formulation.

SLAM names a mapping/localization problem, not one mandatory training paradigm. Geometry or probabilistic state estimation need not constitute unsupervised ML; the source list is application shorthand.
The actual taxonomy page says nature of the task and type of feedback, and lists supervised, unsupervised and reinforcement learning.
The diagram/text defines feature 0 as force and feature 1 as slip. Grasp class 0 success and class 1 failure are outputs, not input colors.
The actual new star is in the blue region, labeled class 0. The accompanying grasp interpretation maps that label to success.
Terrain names are categorical even if encoded as integers. Grip force is a continuous quantitative prediction, so the two tasks are classification and regression.
The source pedestrian/cyclist/vehicle example has three categorical alternatives, hence multiclass classification.
The regression column contains linear regression, Ridge and SVR and reports MSE, MAE and R². The other bundles are class-prediction methods/metrics.
Despite its name, logistic regression appears in the classification list on the source table.
The source 1NN flow stores labeled X,y, receives a new query, finds the closest stored point and returns that point’s class.
The labeled d1 arrow reaches the red class-1 triangle and is shorter than d2 to blue class 0. 1NN selects class 1, not a global majority.
With an explicitly scaled space, the Euclidean calculation is sqrt(3²+4²)=5, not Manhattan distance 7 or squared distance 25.
Two of the three equally weighted labels are 1, so the plurality/majority result is class 1, not the numeric vote count or mean.
The displayed boundaries differ for k=1,3,9 and become smoother in this figure. The illustration gives no universal test-accuracy ordering.
k controls the number of neighbors consulted per query. It is distinct from the number of classes and number of features.
The source explicitly maps 0 to smooth floor, 1 to gravel and 2 to grass. The medium-vibration class is 2, not numeric label order.
The feature headings are speed in m/s and vibration in Hz, and the target is terrain class.
The actual numeric array has six samples, each with two entries; the target array has six scalar entries, giving (6,2) and (6,).
The fifth listed row is [0.9,30] and the fifth target is 2, mapped to grass.
The squared raw distances to the six rows are 2704.09,2500.25,4.01,9.04,1024.04,729.09. The minimum is row [0.8,60], with sqrt(4.01)=2.00249844.
The nearest row’s label is 1. The source dictionary maps 1 to the exact string Gravel (Red).
The estimator input is a two-dimensional one-sample batch; predict produces a one-element label array, and [0] extracts its first label, not label zero.
A returned label is a prediction. With no known target for this query, its correctness and a test-set accuracy cannot be measured.

The printed code has no scaling transformation. Raw squared distances add numerically disparate speed and frequency differences, so frequency can dominate. The units are not standardized automatically.

The observed top region is purple and the source says Gravel (Red); the bottom region looks red but is labeled smooth floor. Numeric label mapping and the explicit class labels determine meaning, not the conflicting color word.
The source imports NumPy for numeric arrays, matplotlib.pyplot and ListedColormap for plotting, and KNeighborsClassifier for the estimator.
The source says weights w and intercept b are learned parameters; x contains one sample’s observed features and y_hat is the prediction.
The dot product plus intercept is 2*3+(-1)*4+0.5=2.5.
Inclusive zero-based indices 0 through p count p+1 entries. Exactly p features use 0 through p-1; the slide wording is off by one.
OLS is a least-squares fitting criterion, not every possible fitting procedure for a linear model. Ridge on p787 is already a counterexample to the universal synonym.
Prediction-minus-target residuals are [1,-1,-1]. Squared residuals are [1,1,1], so SSE=3 and MSE=3/3=1. The source labels a sum as a mean.
For a fixed positive sample count, dividing SSE by n multiplies it by a positive constant independent of parameters, preserving minimizers and objective ordering.
The fitted line is not an interpolating path through all points. It is chosen to reduce aggregate squared prediction residuals, despite nonzero individual residuals.

The arrows depict iterative fitting but do not prove an exclusive solver. The same quadratic least-squares objective also admits direct linear-algebra methods under their usual rank/solution qualifications.
The table grasp-success row explicitly pairs point cloud plus gripper pose with success/failure.
The table depth-image row outputs 3D joint coordinates, a regression target; the remaining choices produce category names.
The table object-recognition row uses image pixels→object class, and the actuator-fault row uses torque/velocity time series→fault type.

Samples-as-rows/features-as-columns is the tabular arrangement illustrated here, not the only raw data structure. Images, sequences and graphs can have structured encodings; targets are not automatically extra input columns.

preRevealQualityNotes: Many stems/options merge ordinary prose with quantities or identifiers; restore normal spacing with versioned changes.
Several distractors are implausible universal guarantees or unrelated mechanisms rather than credible misconceptions.
The source nearest-neighbor similarity assumption merits a direct bounded coverage item; existing questions test workflow and distance but not the premise behind distance-based label transfer.
The SLAM/OLS/MSE/indexing/palette/tabular-representation source qualifications must remain explicit rather than declaring the whole source corrected.
